title: Ollie Watkins ‘expected’ to be dropped from England squad after drop in form
content:
Aston Villa forward Ollie Watkins has acknowledged he “expected” to be dropped from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad after a difficult run of form.

Watkins scored his 10th goal of the season in all competitions during Villa’s 2-0 victory against West Ham on Sunday and was named player of the match.

The 30-year-old’s performance was timely given that, he admitted, recent form “hasn’t been great.”

Watkins has provoked frustration from Villa supporters this season, owing to regular missed chances and struggling to return to his physical best since his peak 2023-24 season, where he averaged a goal every 160 minutes.

Before West Ham’s visit, Watkins had scored nine goals in 42 appearances, working out at a rate of a goal every 309 minutes.

Earlier in the week, Tuchel had named a 35-man squad for England’s upcoming friendlies against Uruguay and Japan, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Dominic Solanke returning to the group at the expense of Watkins.

“Everyone wants to play for their country but I expected that (to be dropped),” Watkins told Sky Sports after Sunday’s win. “My form hasn’t been that great, but I know what I can do. Everyone knows what I can do when I’ve got on an England shirt.

“I feel like I’ve done myself some favours. I feel like I’ve always performed well and I know what I can bring to the team.

“I’m capable of going on a long goalscoring run, so I’m not ruling myself out for that (the World Cup).”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Villa manager Unai Emery defended his striker, praising his display and insisted he could work his way back into the international picture.

“He is a fighter,” said Emery. “Three years ago, he was not in the national team when he deserved to be there. He must recover his fighting way. When he does his task, his numbers are coming, like today.

“Today he fought with the centre-back and he got duels and won them. He held the ball up and played safe passes. He got in the box to threaten them. He did a fantastic, fantastic job.”

Villa’s victory strengthened their position in the Champions League race, moving six points clear of sixth-placed Chelsea.
